title: 2 Peter Chapter 2 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Peter chapter 2 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Peter Chapter 2 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Peter Chapter 2.

questions.question: In 2 Peter 2, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Lot vexed with the filthy conversation
questions.explanation: This is the first event mentioned in the chapter, indicating the presence of false prophets among the people.

questions.question: What shall many follow according to 2 Peter 2:2?
questions.explanation: The verse states that many shall follow their pernicious ways.

questions.question: According to 2 Peter 2:3, how will false teachers make merchandise of you?
questions.explanation: The verse explains that through covetousness they shall make merchandise of you with feigned words.

questions.question: What happened to the angels that sinned according to 2 Peter 2:4?
options: They were cast down to hell
questions.correctAnswer: They were cast down to hell
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that God cast down the angels that sinned to hell.

questions.question: Who did God save from the old world as mentioned in 2 Peter 2:5?
questions.explanation: The verse refers to Noah as the one saved from the flood upon the world of the ungodly.

questions.question: What cities did God turn into ashes according to 2 Peter 2:6?
questions.explanation: The text specifically mentions that God turned the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes.

questions.question: Who was delivered from the wicked according to 2 Peter 2:7?
questions.explanation: The verse states that just Lot was delivered, indicating his righteousness amidst the wicked.

questions.question: What was Lot vexed by according to 2 Peter 2:7?
questions.explanation: The verse mentions that Lot was vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked.

questions.question: According to 2 Peter 2:8, what was vexing Lot's soul?
questions.explanation: The verse states that Lot was vexed by their unlawful deeds from day to day.

questions.question: What is said about the judgment of false teachers in 2 Peter 2:3?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that their judgment now of a long time lingers not.

questions.question: What does 2 Peter 2:1 imply about false teachers?
questions.explanation: The verse states that false teachers shall bring in damnable heresies, even denying the Lord that bought them.

questions.question: True or False: False prophets were present among the people according to 2 Peter 2:1.
questions.explanation: The verse states that there were false prophets among the people.

questions.question: True or False: Lot was a preacher of righteousness according to 2 Peter 2:5.
questions.explanation: The verse refers to Noah as a preacher of righteousness, not Lot.

questions.question: True or False: The text states that the old world was saved from judgment.
questions.explanation: The text states that God spared not the old world, indicating it was not saved but judged.

questions.question: True or False: Sodom and Gomorrha are described as cities that were praised in 2 Peter 2:6.
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that Sodom and Gomorrha were condemned and turned into ashes, not praised.

medium.title: 2 Peter Chapter 2 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Peter Chapter 2 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to 2 Peter 2:9, what does the Lord know how to do?
options: Deliver the godly out of temptations
questions.correctAnswer: Deliver the godly out of temptations
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:9 states that the Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptations and to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished.

questions.question: What does 2 Peter 2:10 promise will happen if someone walks after the flesh in the lust of uncleanness as described in 2 Peter 2:9?
options: They will be reserved unto the day of judgment to be punished
They will be delivered from all troubles
They will be praised among believers
questions.correctAnswer: They will be reserved unto the day of judgment to be punished
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:9-10 show a contrast: the Lord delivers the godly from temptations but reserves the unjust, including those walking after the flesh in lust, unto the day of judgment to be punished.

questions.question: How do the false teachers described in 2 Peter 2:12 behave according to their understanding?
options: Speak evil of the things they understand not
questions.correctAnswer: Speak evil of the things they understand not
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:12 describes these false teachers as natural brute beasts who speak evil of things they do not understand and will perish in their own corruption.

questions.question: What is the connection between 2 Peter 2:14 and 2 Peter 2:13 regarding the character of false teachers?
options: Both describe them as corrupt and deceitful with unstable souls
Both warn believers to follow them
questions.correctAnswer: Both describe them as corrupt and deceitful with unstable souls
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:13 speaks of spots and blemishes who deceive, while verse 14 describes them as having eyes full of adultery and unstable souls, highlighting their corrupt nature.

questions.question: What practical lesson can believers learn from 2 Peter 2:9 about facing temptations?
options: Trust that the Lord will deliver the godly out of temptations
Rely only on personal strength to overcome temptation
Ignore temptations as they are insignificant
questions.correctAnswer: Trust that the Lord will deliver the godly out of temptations
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:9 reassures believers that the Lord knows how to deliver the godly out of temptations, encouraging faith and trust in God during trials.

questions.question: According to 2 Peter 2:11, how do angels compare with false teachers in their behavior?
options: Angels do not bring railing accusation against dignities
Angels are more presumptuous than false teachers
Angels speak evil of dignities openly
Angels follow the flesh in the lust of uncleanness
questions.correctAnswer: Angels do not bring railing accusation against dignities
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:11 points out that angels, who are greater in power and might, do not bring railing accusations against dignities before the Lord, unlike the false teachers.

questions.question: What does 2 Peter 2:15 say about those who follow the way of Balaam?
options: They have forsaken the right way and gone astray
They are praised for their faithfulness
They are examples of righteous living
They bring blessings to the church
questions.correctAnswer: They have forsaken the right way and gone astray
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:15 describes those who follow the way of Balaam as having forsaken the right way and gone astray, motivated by love of unrighteous wages.

questions.question: How does 2 Peter 2:16 illustrate God's judgment on Balaam's iniquity?
options: By the dumb ass speaking with man's voice forbidding the prophet's madness
By Balaam being forgiven without rebuke
questions.correctAnswer: By the dumb ass speaking with man's voice forbidding the prophet's madness
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:16 explains that Balaam was rebuked for his iniquity when his dumb ass spoke with man's voice and forbade his madness.

questions.question: What warning does 2 Peter 2:14 give about the spiritual state of certain false teachers?
options: They have eyes full of adultery and cannot cease from sin
They are pure and stable in faith
They are humble and teach with gentleness
questions.correctAnswer: They have eyes full of adultery and cannot cease from sin
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:14 warns that these false teachers have eyes full of adultery, cannot cease from sin, and deceive unstable souls through covetous practices.

questions.question: According to 2 Peter 2:13, what do false teachers count as pleasure?
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:13 indicates that false teachers count it pleasure to riot in the daytime, behaving corruptly and deceitfully.

questions.question: What is the fate of those described as 'natural brute beasts' in 2 Peter 2:12?
options: They shall utterly perish in their own corruption
They shall be exalted in the church
They shall be forgiven without repentance
They shall be delivered from judgment
questions.correctAnswer: They shall utterly perish in their own corruption
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:12 states that these natural brute beasts, who speak evil of what they do not understand, shall utterly perish in their own corruption.

questions.question: How does 2 Peter 2:10 describe the attitude of those who despise government?
options: Presumptuous, self-willed, and not afraid to speak evil of dignities
questions.correctAnswer: Presumptuous, self-willed, and not afraid to speak evil of dignities
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:10 describes such individuals as presumptuous, self-willed, and lacking fear in speaking evil of dignities, showing their rebellious nature.

questions.question: What does 2 Peter 2:9 suggest about God's justice toward the unjust?
options: God reserves the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished
God delivers the unjust from temptation
questions.correctAnswer: God reserves the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:9 clearly says the Lord reserves the unjust until the day of judgment to be punished, showing His commitment to justice.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Peter 2:11, angels bring railing accusations against dignities before the Lord.
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:11 states that angels, which are greater in power and might, do not bring railing accusations against dignities before the Lord.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Peter 2:15 commends those who follow the way of Balaam for their love of righteousness.
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:15 condemns those following Balaam's way for forsaking the right way and going astray, loving the wages of unrighteousness, not righteousness.

hard.title: 2 Peter Chapter 2 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Peter Chapter 2.

questions.question: What are false teachers compared to in 2 Peter 2:17?
questions.explanation: This is stated in 2 Peter 2:17 where it describes false teachers as 'wells without water'.

questions.question: According to 2 Peter 2:18, how do false teachers allure those who have escaped error?
options: Through great swelling words of vanity
questions.correctAnswer: Through great swelling words of vanity
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:18 mentions false teachers allure others 'through great swelling words of vanity'.

questions.question: What do false teachers promise according to 2 Peter 2:19?
questions.explanation: In 2 Peter 2:19, it states they promise liberty, but are actually servants of corruption.

questions.question: What is said to be worse than the beginning for those who are overcome again by the world in 2 Peter 2:20?
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:20 indicates that the latter end is worse for those who return to pollutions than their initial state.

questions.question: What proverb is referenced in 2 Peter 2:22?
options: The lion will lay with the lamb
The dog is turned to his own vomit again
questions.correctAnswer: The dog is turned to his own vomit again
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:22 refers to the proverb 'The dog is turned to his own vomit again' to illustrate the folly of returning to sin.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'ἀλήθεια' (aletheia) in 2 Peter 2:2 mean?
questions.explanation: 'ἀλήθεια' (aletheia) is the Greek word for 'truth', as seen in the context of false teachers causing it to be evil spoken of in 2 Peter 2:2.

questions.question: Which literary device is used in 2 Peter 2:19 when discussing the concept of bondage?
questions.explanation: The discussion of bondage in 2 Peter 2:19 uses metaphor to illustrate the spiritual condition of those deceived by false teachers.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of false teachers in 2 Peter 2:1?
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:15 warns of false prophets, echoing the theme found in 2 Peter 2:1 about false teachers.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the idea of returning to sin as seen in 2 Peter 2:22?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 26:11 parallels the idea of returning to sin, similar to the message in 2 Peter 2:22 regarding the dog returning to its vomit.

questions.question: What comes before 2 Peter 2:21?
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:21 follows directly after 2 Peter 2:20, which discusses the consequences of being entangled again.

questions.question: What comes after 2 Peter 2:22?
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:22 is followed by 2 Peter 2:23, which continues the discussion on the consequences of false teachings.

questions.question: The statement 'they are not afraid to speak evil of dignities' in 2 Peter 2:10 suggests what about false teachers?
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:10 indicates that false teachers are 'presumptuous' and 'self-willed', showing their disregard for authority.

questions.question: In 2 Peter 2:6, the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrha serves as what literary device?
questions.explanation: The destruction of Sodom and Gomorrha in 2 Peter 2:6 serves as a typological warning for those who live ungodly lives.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Peter 2:21, knowing the way of righteousness is beneficial regardless of one's actions.
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:21 states it is better not to have known the way of righteousness than to turn away after knowing it.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Peter 2:19 indicates that those who are overcome by false teachers are actually brought into bondage.
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:19 explains that those who are overcome by false teachers are indeed brought into bondage, reflecting their servitude to corruption.

theological.title: 2 Peter Chapter 2 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Peter Chapter 2 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Peter 2:1 teach about human sin?
options: False teachers bring in damnable heresies denying the Lord
All humans are inherently righteous before God
Sin is only external behavior without doctrinal impact
Salvation can be earned through works
questions.correctAnswer: False teachers bring in damnable heresies denying the Lord
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:1 teaches that false teachers introduce destructive heresies, even denying the Lord who bought them, highlighting the sinfulness of such doctrinal error.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Peter 2:4 teach about divine judgment?
options: God judges even fallen angels by casting them into chains of darkness
Angels are exempt from God's judgment
God forgives all sin without judgment
Judgment is reserved only for human beings
questions.correctAnswer: God judges even fallen angels by casting them into chains of darkness
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:4 explains that God did not spare the angels who sinned but cast them into hell and chains of darkness reserved for judgment, teaching divine justice extends beyond humans.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Peter 2:9 teach about God's providence in salvation?
options: The Lord knows how to deliver the godly out of temptations and reserve the unjust for judgment
God is unaware of human suffering
Salvation is random and not under God's control
All are delivered regardless of their moral state
questions.correctAnswer: The Lord knows how to deliver the godly out of temptations and reserve the unjust for judgment
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:9 teaches God's providential care in delivering the godly from temptation and reserving the unjust for punishment, affirming both divine sovereignty and justice.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does verse 2 Peter 2:3 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:3 speaks of the judgment and damnation of false teachers that does not slumber, highlighting God's attribute of justice.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does verse 2 Peter 2:9 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:9 reveals God's sovereign control in delivering the godly and reserving the unjust for judgment, demonstrating divine sovereignty.

questions.question: How does 2 Peter 2:5 connect to the broader biblical theme of judgment and salvation?
options: By highlighting Noah as a preacher of righteousness who was saved from the flood
By denying the reality of the flood account
By teaching universal salvation irrespective of righteousness
By emphasizing human effort over divine intervention
questions.correctAnswer: By highlighting Noah as a preacher of righteousness who was saved from the flood
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:5 connects to the biblical theme of judgment and salvation by showing God saving Noah, a preacher of righteousness, amidst judgment on the ungodly world.

questions.question: How does the condemnation of Sodom and Gomorrah in 2 Peter 2:6 fulfill Old Testament typology?
options: They serve as examples of God's judgment on ungodliness for all generations
They illustrate God's abandonment of His covenant people
They symbolize God's acceptance of sin
They demonstrate the futility of repentance
questions.correctAnswer: They serve as examples of God's judgment on ungodliness for all generations
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:6 refers to Sodom and Gomorrah as examples of judgment on ungodliness, fulfilling typology of divine punishment for persistent sin.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 2 Peter 2:10 and 2 Peter 2:11 teach about human sin and angelic behavior?
options: Some humans act presumptuously and blaspheme, unlike angels who do not bring accusations against dignities
Humans and angels are equal in sinfulness and accusation
Angels frequently accuse humans before God
Humans are incapable of sin compared to angels
questions.correctAnswer: Some humans act presumptuously and blaspheme, unlike angels who do not bring accusations against dignities
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:10-11 contrasts presumptuous, self-willed humans who speak evil of dignities with angels who do not bring railing accusations, teaching about differing behaviors in sin and reverence.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 2 Peter 2:20 and 2 Peter 2:21 teach about apostasy?
options: Those who fall away after knowing Christ experience a worse end than before
Once saved, always saved without any risk of falling away
Apostasy improves a person's spiritual condition
questions.correctAnswer: Those who fall away after knowing Christ experience a worse end than before
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:20-21 teaches that those who escape worldly pollutions through Christ but then become entangled again experience a worse condition, emphasizing the seriousness of apostasy.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 2 Peter 2:7 and 2 Peter 2:8 teach about the righteous living in an ungodly environment?
options: The righteous are vexed by the sinful behavior around them, affecting their souls
The righteous are unaffected by the sinfulness of others
God abandons the righteous in ungodly surroundings
The righteous become sinful by association
questions.correctAnswer: The righteous are vexed by the sinful behavior around them, affecting their souls
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:7-8 describes Lot as righteous yet vexed daily by the unlawful deeds around him, teaching about the spiritual burden of living among the wicked.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 2 Peter 2:13 and 2 Peter 2:14 teach about false teachers' character and influence?
options: They are spots and blemishes who beguile unstable souls through covetousness and unceasing sin
They are holy and pure examples to the church
They teach with humility and truth
They lead others to repentance and faith
questions.correctAnswer: They are spots and blemishes who beguile unstable souls through covetousness and unceasing sin
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:13-14 depict false teachers as corrupt, sinful, and deceptive, influencing unstable souls through greed and ongoing sinfulness.

questions.question: Sceptics claim 2 Peter 2:15-16 endorses false prophecy because Balaam was not rebuked. What does 2 Peter 2:15-16 actually teach?
options: Balaam was rebuked for his iniquity, illustrating divine judgment on false teachers
Balaam's prophecy was wholly accepted as true
False teachers are never held accountable
Balaam's donkey did not speak, so the story is invalid
questions.correctAnswer: Balaam was rebuked for his iniquity, illustrating divine judgment on false teachers
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:15-16 clearly states Balaam was rebuked for his sin, with even the donkey speaking to forbid his madness, illustrating God's judgment on corrupt teachers.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Peter 2:17 teach about the nature of false teachers?
options: False teachers are like wells without water and clouds carried with a tempest, reserved for darkness
False teachers provide abundant spiritual nourishment
False teachers are stable and trustworthy
False teachers have no judgment awaiting them
questions.correctAnswer: False teachers are like wells without water and clouds carried with a tempest, reserved for darkness
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:17 uses metaphorical language to teach that false teachers are empty and unstable, destined for eternal darkness.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Peter 2:22 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:22 illustrates the defilement and folly of turning back to sin, implicitly affirming God's holiness as the standard that condemns such behavior.

questions.question: How does 2 Peter 2:18 contribute to the narrative arc of temptation and deception in salvation history?
options: It shows false teachers alluring those escaped from error through fleshly lusts and vanity
It declares all temptations are from God directly
It teaches that deception only affects the ungodly
It states that lust has no influence on believers
questions.correctAnswer: It shows false teachers alluring those escaped from error through fleshly lusts and vanity
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:18 explains how false teachers use enticing words to lure those who had escaped error, illustrating the ongoing danger of deception in salvation history.
